title: Monitoring that runs: a model in use read window by window from its own logs, against its holdout (34.10)
request: The owner asked to finish Phase 10 without stopping. The plan (docs/guides/PHASE10_ABILITIES_PLAN.md, 34.10) asks for monitor_log over the prediction and outcome logs: drift on each batch, live performance once outcomes arrive with the label delay respected, the service's /monitor report, alerts as events.
spec: dclab_core/live.py: BatchProfile v1 (inputs as bin shares of twenty rows or more, never a value), Profiler, monitor_log (LiveReport v1), reference (the holdout's measure and interval); the exported service writes profiles.jsonl and alerts.jsonl and answers GET /monitor.
plan: read the prediction log (34.9) and the monitoring plan (30.15): the log holds no input value, so inputs need their own record
profiles: each column's share in the plan's bins, gathered as rows are scored
windows by day, week or batch; the score's PSI and the flagged share as monitoring.monitor reads them
live performance from outcomes known by the reading, with an interval, against the holdout's
simulate ten days with a planted drift and a label delay; measure over twenty seeds
the service: profiles, the monitor route, alerts kept

decisions.decision: Watch the inputs through bin shares gathered over at least twenty rows, never linked to a request
decisions.why: the prediction log promises no input value; a profile of one row would be that row binned

decisions.decision: Read a window's performance only once it is mature (most of its rows labelled, or a stated label horizon past)
decisions.why: outcomes of flagged rows often arrive first; read early, an undrifted day looked worse than the holdout

decisions.decision: One window worse than the holdout is a warning; two running are an alert
decisions.why: measured: one window alone was worse by chance in about 2 of 120, a false alarm several times a year on daily windows

decisions.decision: Alerts as events are kept by the service in alerts.jsonl; the main product records them as its own
decisions.why: the owner chose that the main product runs customer models; the exported service is the working reference

change: dclab_core/live.py (new); contracts.py and adapters/conformance.py (registered); schemas; dclab_rnd/studio/service.py (live_reference over groups, README, a longer request timeout); service_template scorer.py (monitoring_plan, monitoring_frame, a scalar missing check), serve_log.py (Profiler, monitor, alerts), app.py (GET /monitor); tests/test_core_live.py (new), tests/test_service_export.py (extended).

findings.defect: a performance alert on one window rang falsely
findings.scenario: twenty simulated runs with drift planted on day six: an earlier day alerted in 2 of 20
findings.cause: two 90% intervals fail to overlap by chance now and then; with daily windows that happens often
findings.fix: one worse window is a warning, two running an alert; the planted drift stayed the first alert in 20 of 20 and no run alerted early
findings.impact: a team paged for nothing every few weeks
alternatives: a 99% interval: slower to see a real drop

findings.defect: a window was judged on its first outcomes, which were the flagged rows
findings.scenario: flagged rows labelled after a day and the rest after thirty: an undrifted day read 0.69 against a holdout of 0.82 and alerted
findings.cause: a window was read as soon as a hundred outcomes were known, whatever share of its rows they were
findings.fix: a window is read once mature: at least nine in ten of its rows labelled, or a stated label horizon past its end
findings.impact: fraud monitoring would alert every day on a healthy model

findings.defect: a small request wrote its row's bins to the profile log
findings.scenario: a one-row prediction wrote shares of zero and one, the row binned, joined to its key through the request
findings.cause: a profile was written per request, with the request's id
findings.fix: profiles gather twenty rows or more in the process and carry no request id; the contract refuses fewer rows
findings.impact: a column with few values would be readable per row from the logs
alternatives: add noise to small profiles: harder to read and still close to the row

findings.defect: importing the monitoring module first failed
findings.scenario: a fresh interpreter importing dclab_core.monitoring met a half-made module
findings.cause: the contracts module imports the live module at its end, which imported names from monitoring while it was loading
findings.fix: the live module imports the monitoring and serving modules themselves and reads their names at call time
findings.impact: the main product would fail at start if it imports monitoring first

findings.scenario: a column no longer sent stayed stable; a reading as of a past moment saw later rows; a worse window of a few rows was hidden; another model's lines in a shared folder were read; a list value failed a request after it was logged; the monitor ran past a request's timeout on a large log
findings.cause: absent columns were skipped, the cut filtered outcomes only, the few-rows status came first, no model filter, a vector missing check, a ranking loop in Python
findings.fix: an absent column counts as missing; the cut applies to predictions, profiles and recorded outcomes; alerts come before the few-rows status; only this model and fit are read; profiling never fails a request; the ranking is vectorised and the timeout longer
findings.impact: missed drifts, readings that knew the future, and a monitor that failed under load

measurements.name: planted drift over twenty simulated runs
measurements.gate: the planted drift is the first alert and no earlier day alerts; undrifted days agree with the holdout within the intervals
measurements.result: first alert on the drift day in 20 of 20, none earlier; undrifted windows within in 117 of 120; with flagged rows labelled first, 0 false alerts in 20
measurements.next: the main product's monitoring job reads its own logs through it
limits: simulated rows and one model family
multiclass and regression services not tested end to end

outcome: A model in use can be read window by window from its own logs: the inputs and the score against training, the flagged share, and performance once its outcomes are known, with alerts kept and no value of a row ever written.
lessons: A window is not known until its outcomes are: the first outcomes are rarely a fair sample.
An aggregate of one row is the row.
A module that registers itself at the end of another must not take names from modules that may still be loading.
risks: profiles in a process are lost when it stops before twenty rows
a plan from an older fit read against a newer fit's rows
